Q2_convergence.question: Is the endpoint convergence real or an artifact of averaging?

seq.cancellation_note: mean_abs_err / abs_err_of_the_mean. A value near 1 means the cells really are all near c*; a large value means the mean is close only because per-cell errors cancel in sign.

stage_index_control.note: For each stage index k, the cross-cell mean of c and the cross-cell mean of |c - c*|. If k=6 is not distinguished, the endpoint is not a special place -- the arm simply straddles c* throughout.

Q3_return_or_arrive.question: Does the criterion return, or does it happen to end near the bound?

definitions.net_to_gross: |c_end - c_base| / Sigma|dc|. 1.0 = a straight monotone march; low = the path doubled back on itself.
definitions.crossings: sign changes of (c_k - c_end) over k=1..N-1: how many times the trajectory crossed the level it ends at.
definitions.endpoint_rank: rank of c_end among the cell's N visited criteria (1 = most liberal). Interior rank => it came back; rank 1 or N => it ended at an extreme of its own path.
definitions.best_earlier_err: min over k<N of |c_k - c*|: did the cell pass closer to the target earlier and then move away?

joint.note: n<4: per-cell values only, no interval.

Q4_what_is_drift_worth.question: How much POPE F1 is the mid-sequence drift actually worth?

definitions.worst_drift_stage: argmax over ALL stages k of |c_k - c*| (pre-specified primary).
definitions.worst_drift_stage_mid: argmax over k < N of |c_k - c*| -- the mid-sequence restriction, which is the quantity the question asks about when the endpoint is itself well placed.
definitions.f1_gap: endpoint F1 minus F1 at that stage. Positive = the drifted stage was WORSE than the endpoint, i.e. the drift cost accuracy.
